To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IGF-I stimulates proliferation of brown adipocytes and induces expression of early and later growth-regulated genes.
IGF-I, as a mitogen, is involved in the expression of growth-related and differentiation-related genes in fetal rat brown cells.
IGF-I stimulates the growth and differentiation of fetal rat brown adipocyte cells in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the molecular basis of brown adipose tissue growth and function.
the role of IGF-I as an autocrine/paracrine factor in brown adipose tissue (BAT) development, and with its involvement in the differentiation of brown adipocytes.
the study of IGF-I action on brown adipocyte proliferation and differentiation, as a possible mechanism for the control of brown adipocyte number in fetal and adult life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

IGF- I is a mitogen, capable of inducing proliferation and differentiation, and that IGF-I and FCS share a common pathway in the regulation of the expression of genes involved in the control of proliferation and differentiation of fetal rat brown adipose cells.
IGF-I, like other growth factors, is involved in the regulation of proliferation and differentiation of fetal brown adipocytes.
IGF-I acts as a growth factor for fetal brown adipocytes, and that it is also involved in their differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IGF-I, in addition to insulin, is a growth factor capable of inducing the entry of fetal rat brown adipocyte into the cell-cycle, and the expression of growth-regulated genes.
the IGF-I receptor in brown adipocytes is functional and that the IGF-IR signaling is involved in the proliferation and differentiation of brown adipocytes.
IGF-I, in addition to its mitogenic activity, is also able to stimulate the differentiation of brown adipocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IGF-I can act as a mitogen for rat brown adipocytes in culture, and that it may play a role in the regulation of growth and differentiation of brown adipose tissue.
the IGF-1 receptor is expressed in the fetal rat brown adipocyte and that IGF-I can stimulate the proliferation of these cells in a dose- and time-dependent manner.
the IGF-IR signaling pathway is a major determinant in brown adipocyte development, proliferation and differentiation.
